scene: scene 4 — The storekeeper counts it, and the short count is evidence
detail: SHP-2026-0909 is in two mutually exclusive states on one screen. In 'Arriving at your sites' it reads status 'Delivered' with an active 'Record the count' button — i.e. no receipt taken. In 'Short counts you have raised' twelve rows below it reads ADVISED 900 / YOU COUNTED 840 / SHORT 60 — i.e. the receipt was taken — and 840 is already booked as Monguno's on-hand on the sites page. The 'Awaiting your count' tile counts it, so that tile reads 10 when the true figure is 9. A first-time user reproducing the flow would press 'Record the count' on a consignment the app has already counted, and the contradiction lands squarely on the scene's own thesis that the difference 'becomes a discrepancy the moment it is recorded'.
fix_recommendation: Derive the row action and the tile from one receipt-status field: once a receipt is recorded the row reads 'Counted — 60 short' with a link to the discrepancy instead of the 'Record the count' CTA, and the 'Awaiting your count' tile reads 9.

scene: scene 2 — Inbound supply, in the calendar they plan in
detail: scroll_to('css:.card:has-text("Distribution calendar")') overshot and landed the frame mid-table on the Jul 31 Mafa row. The card title, the load-bearing subtitle that reconciles 'stock on the day' against the cover table below, the entire column-header row (DISTRIBUTION DAY / SITE / CHILDREN EXPECTED / CARTONS REQUIRED / STOCK ON THE DAY / COVER) and the Jul 31 Askira 'at risk' row the spec itself names as an exemplar are all above the viewport. The scene is narrated over six unlabelled numeric columns, and the header band would have fit.
fix_recommendation: Retarget the scroll to the card's heading or the table's thead (scroll-margin on .card h3) and add a settle-hold, so title, subtitle, column headers and the Jul 31 Askira / Aug 1 Biu rows are all in frame when they are spoken about.

scene: scene 5 — Zara raises a shortfall, and the centre answers
detail: The modal is the subject of this scene's densest narration — 'the site, the date, the children affected, the cartons short' plus the pre-filled-from-the-site's-own-projection claim — and it appears in neither frame. scene_5_before.png is the previous scene's Receiving page, so the before/after pair brackets the navigation rather than the act. The toast is uncaptured too, and the one element that visibly changed on the sites page (Kukawa's 'Raise a shortfall' button becoming 'Raised Jul 28, 2026') is scrolled off the top of the after-frame, whose upper third instead shows the three healthiest sites (Ngala 4, Gwoza 4.5, Dikwa 5.5 weeks, all green). The trace confirms the act genuinely happened — 13 actions, all ok:true — so this is purely a capture-scripting miss.
fix_recommendation: Add a capture beat during the existing hold while the modal is open (before the 'Raise it' click), and after the toast scroll_to Kukawa's cover row so the button-to-state change is on camera before the scene settles on the shortfalls card.

scene: scene 2 — Inbound supply, in the calendar they plan in
detail: Three of the four specific facts the narration asserts are falsified by the rendered page, and a fourth is unevidenced. (1) 'Next Tuesday at Monguno needs eight hundred cartons' — Monguno's CARTONS REQUIRED is 532 on both its rows; 840 is the STOCK ON THE DAY column, so supply has been quoted as demand, and no row anywhere requires ~800. (2) 'Next Tuesday' — the page's as-of date is Tue Jul 28 2026 and Monguno's distributions fall on Aug 2 and Aug 9, both Sundays; the Tuesday row is Gwoza. (3) 'The Thursday distribution at Kukawa reads as at risk' — the in-frame Thursday Kukawa row (Aug 6) reads 'covered' (235 required / 375 stock); the at-risk Kukawa is Aug 13, below the fold. (4) 'the one after it has nothing assigned to it at all' — no such row exists; Aug 13 is Kukawa's last row and the only 'uncovered' row on the entire page is Biu, Aug 1. The spec's own show block ('Askira at risk, and Biu with nothing assigned') matches the screen exactly, so the drift is in the narrative lock, not the data.
fix_recommendation: Re-narrate scene 2 from the captured page text rather than a prior dataset — e.g. 'Friday at Askira needs 63 cartons; 38 are on the shelf with 94 more due, so it reads at risk. Saturday at Biu has nothing assigned to it at all. Everything else next week is covered.' — then re-render. Adopt a standing rule that every narrated figure is quoted from scene_N_page_text.json.

scene: scene 5 — Zara raises a shortfall, and the centre answers
detail: Three narrated elements have no on-screen referent. (1) 'the cartons short' is named as a field of the record, but 'Shortfalls you have raised' has only RAISED / SITE / CHILDREN AFFECTED / NEEDED BY / STATUS — the unit the whole supply chain is denominated in is dropped, and the product's own Receiving screen proves it can carry it ('SHORT 60'). (2) 'it lands in the OES command centre ranked against every other exception by the children behind it' — no queue, rank, position, SLA or OES surface appears anywhere; the record's entire state is an amber 'open' pill. (3) 'marked as raised by Komadugu rather than derived centrally' — there is no source or provenance field on the record; only the card title implies partner origin. Separately, CHILDREN AFFECTED 94 is not reconstructable for Kukawa: its rows book 235 children, the nearest arithmetic is 235 − 140 = 95, and 94 is exactly what a different site (Biu) books on Aug 1 and Aug 8, so a viewer hunting the provenance of 94 lands on the wrong site.
fix_recommendation: Instantiate rather than trim: add a CARTONS SHORT column (mirroring Receiving's SHORT), a SOURCE badge reading 'Raised by Komadugu', and a queue-position field ('#2 of 14 open exceptions by children affected'); and derive CHILDREN AFFECTED from the site's own calendar with the derivation in an info bubble so the number reconciles with the row it came from.

scene: scene 4 — The storekeeper counts it, and the short count is evidence
detail: The core numbers do check out — 900 advised, 840 counted, 60 short and '60 lose a full course' are all literally on screen, and 'labelled as hand-keyed' maps to the visible 'Entered by hand' pill. But the scene's pivot is narrated over footage that contradicts it: 'that difference becomes a discrepancy the moment it is recorded' is spoken over a row whose own status and CTA say the count has not been recorded, and the action trace performs no receipt at all (a nav click plus two camera moves; ten 'Record the count' buttons sit unpressed). 'records the receipt from a phone' has no phone, no mobile viewport and no capture form anywhere in the run, and 'at the loading bay' is asserted only.
fix_recommendation: Perform the act on camera: click 'Record the count' on SHP-2026-0909, enter 840, submit, and let the discrepancy card appear as the result — then 900/840/60 is demonstrated rather than pre-baked. If the low-tech tier is to survive the claim, capture that form at a phone viewport.

scene: scene 4 — The storekeeper counts it, and the short count is evidence (emblematic; scored against the whole walkthrough)
detail: The walkthrough shows real work at real scale — eleven sites, twenty-two dated distributions, a 60-carton short against a named despatch advice converted to 60 children denied a full course, a batch resolving to 22 MUAC series across 511 children fed. A skeptic would not call it a toy. But two beats stop one step short of the value they sell. Scene 4 demonstrates reconciliation as a subtraction and never shows the discrepancy's downstream life: no supplier acknowledgement, no dispute state, no resolution, and the 'ranked against every other exception' claim asserted only in prose. Scene 5 sells triage across a pool of exceptions while showing only the partner's own two-row list. A skeptical buyer can fairly ask 'and then what happens?' — the answer is off camera in both cases.
fix_recommendation: Show the exception's downstream life inside the partner's own surface: give a raised short count / shortfall a lifecycle (Raised → Acknowledged by supplier → Resolved) with a timestamp and counterparty, and a visible position among open exceptions. The value of raising a discrepancy is what happens after the number is raised, and right now the demo ends at the number.

scene: scene 4 — The storekeeper counts it, and the short count is evidence
detail: The 'evidence, not dispute' half lands fast and well — the YOU COUNTED column, the partner badge, 'Short counts YOU have raised', and the children-affected unit make the who-raised-it point read in seconds. The second half of the concept_claim — 'labelled hand-keyed' — is invisible: the amber 'Entered by hand' pill is identical on all twelve rows including two consignments still in transit, no contrasting provenance value exists anywhere in the view, and the REPORTED BY column header is scrolled out of frame at the exact moment the narration calls the label out. An outsider must ask 'hand-keyed as opposed to what, and why does it matter?'
fix_recommendation: Make the provenance column discriminate in this view — seed at least one consignment from the machine-to-machine tier (e.g. 'From despatch feed') alongside the hand-keyed ones — and add an 'i' bubble on the REPORTED BY header defining each value in one line. A marker only carries information when the reader can see it take a different value.

scene: scene 4 — The storekeeper counts it, and the short count is evidence
detail: Table craft is good — tight alignment, consistent button styling across all ten rows, clean type, generous card whitespace, host chrome intact. Two rubric caps fire. (1) On-screen editorialising: 'A shortfall asserted from a spreadsheet is an opinion. This one was counted beside the pallets.' and 'the count you take is what the figure becomes' put the narrator's argument in the product's own voice, at its own user. Under the OBJECTIVE-DATA standing rule the takeaway on an evidence product should be the data, legibly shown, not a sentence. (2) Non-semantic colour: twelve identical amber 'Entered by hand' pills paint a caution-coloured vertical band over an invariant, unexceptional field while the actual variable data (quantities) stays plain text.
fix_recommendation: Replace the rhetorical subtitles with factual ones ('Counted at the receiving store against the despatch advice'), move the one-carton-equals-one-course definition into an 'i' bubble on the CHILDREN AFFECTED header instead of a paragraph of prose, and demote the uniform provenance pill to neutral grey so amber is reserved for a value that actually varies.

scene: scene 4 — The storekeeper counts it, and the short count is evidence
detail: The scroll_to landed the 'Short counts you have raised' payoff card fully and settled with breathing room — that part is competent. But the frame opens mid-row on a headerless continuation of the shipments table, so every column in the upper half (including the REPORTED BY provenance column the narration is describing) is unlabelled, and the three key-figure tiles the spec's show block names ('2 consignments in transit', '10 awaiting your count', '60 short on receipt') are above the fold and never seen.
fix_recommendation: Add a hold on the key-figure tiles while the narration describes what is inbound, and adjust the scroll offset so the table's header row is in frame when 'labelled as hand-keyed' is spoken.

scene: scene 5 — Zara raises a shortfall, and the centre answers
detail: The 'raise' half is clear and well signposted: a concrete role is named on screen, every site row carries its own 'Raise a shortfall' affordance, and the card subhead states the direction in the product's own words ('Reported upward from this screen, and answered against the same record'). The half that makes the concept new — the central queue, the ranking by children, the partner-raised marking — is carried entirely by the voiceover, so a cold viewer gets 'partner logged a ticket' rather than 'the ground reports upward into a system that can respond'. Compounding it, CHILDREN AFFECTED 94 is the number the ranking is supposedly BY, and it is the one number the viewer cannot reconstruct.
fix_recommendation: Add a SOURCE column reading 'Raised by Komadugu' and a queue-position column ('#2 of 14 by children affected') to 'Shortfalls you have raised'. Two columns turn a spoken claim into a shown one.

scene: scene 5 — Zara raises a shortfall, and the centre answers
detail: The interaction model holds and is genuinely well built — per-row action, a modal pre-filled from the site's own projection, an explicit 'Raise it' submit, a toast, and the button mutating into state ('Raised Jul 24, 2026' / 'Raised Jul 28, 2026') so the same shortfall cannot be raised twice. It stays at 3 because the loop is hand-wavy at both ends: the record drops a field the form captured (cartons short), and the card advertises a return path ('answered against the same record') that has no answered state — both rows are 'open', so the second half of the loop is never instantiated in the demo data.
fix_recommendation: Add CARTONS SHORT to the shortfalls table carrying the value the modal already collects, and seed one acknowledged/answered shortfall in the demo data so both halves of the loop are visible on camera.

scene: scene 5 — Zara raises a shortfall, and the centre answers
detail: The use is real — a site serving 1,016 children a month with 1.6 weeks of cover, escalated from the same screen that computed the projection, replacing a WhatsApp loop. But the value proposition the narration sells is triage across every other exception, and the scene never shows the feature at that scale: the viewer sees the partner's own two-row list and never the pool it is supposedly ranked within. Rubric deduction 'never shows the feature at the scale/complexity where its value would actually be felt: max 3'.
fix_recommendation: Show the raised item against the pool it competes with — even one line on the partner's own record ('ranked 2nd of 14 open exceptions, 94 children') — so the skeptic sees the queue exists rather than being told it does. If the OES side belongs to the next narrative, this scene still needs its partner-visible shadow.

scene: scene 5 — Zara raises a shortfall, and the centre answers
detail: Restrained and coherent — consistent card/subhead pattern, one type scale, semantic colour only, consistent date formatting, method disclosure in a footnote rather than an editorial verdict. Real designer notes keep it at 3: the left nav rail is not sticky, so ~230px (~18% of the frame) is empty white in both frames and a long page loses its navigation entirely; numeric columns are left-aligned (1,627 / 1,761 / 94 / 87) so magnitudes cannot be compared down a column; unit conventions drift between tables ('375 cartons' inline vs a bare '235'); the narrated card is given the least visual weight of the three in frame; and the audit-critical method definitions sit at ~11px grey.
fix_recommendation: Make the left nav rail position:sticky; right-align numeric columns and move units into the column headers; and raise the method footnote to body-adjacent size or promote it into 'i' bubbles on the headers it defines.

scene: scene 2 — Inbound supply, in the calendar they plan in
detail: The concept — inbound supply expressed as distribution-day-at-site rather than a shipment list — is legible from the structure (date, named site, status pill) and the narration names a concrete role. But with the card title, subtitle and column headers all clipped above the viewport, an outsider gets six unlabelled numeric columns and must ask which one is demand and which is supply. The 5-second read is 'a date-and-site list, mostly green'.
fix_recommendation: Make the calendar table's header row sticky within the card so the column names remain on screen at any scroll depth, and move the COVER definition from the card's intro paragraph into an 'i' affordance on the COVER header so the rule travels with the column instead of living in prose that scrolls away.

scene: scene 2 — Inbound supply, in the calendar they plan in
detail: The interaction model holds — one table, one status column, one vocabulary — but the 'at risk' and 'uncovered' states are dead ends: nothing on the row opens the consignment that is or is not coming, which is the next question the state provokes and the exact object the narration talks about. '38 (+94 later)' names an inbound consignment the user cannot resolve. Credit where due: the calendar-vs-cover-table divergence for the same site is explicitly reconciled in the card's own subtitle ('the cover table below counts only what has physically arrived, which is why a site can run dry there and still be covered here') rather than left as a silent contradiction.
fix_recommendation: Make each calendar row expandable to the consignments counted into its STOCK ON THE DAY (id, quantity, ETA, status) so '38 (+94 later)' resolves to a real object.

scene: scene 2 — Inbound supply, in the calendar they plan in
detail: Colour discipline is genuinely good and correctly non-editorialising. The deductions are typographic: all numeric columns are left-aligned so magnitudes cannot be scanned down a column (38 sits above 1,635 looking identical) on a screen whose entire job is quantity comparison; typographic hierarchy is flat with dates, site names and figures at one weight so 22 near-identical rows read as wallpaper; CHILDREN EXPECTED and CARTONS REQUIRED hold byte-identical values in all 22 rows, burning a third of the table width and hiding the one-carton-per-course rule that justifies them; and ~230px of empty left rail pushes the table off-centre.
fix_recommendation: Right-align and tabular-figure the numeric columns, give the site name medium weight and the date a muted treatment so each row has an anchor, and collapse CHILDREN EXPECTED / CARTONS REQUIRED into one column ('63 children · 63 cartons') with the conversion rule as an 'i' bubble on the header.

scene: scene 1 — The organisation that feeds the children sees the least
detail: The four key figures the show block calls 'the whole argument in four numbers' are now fully in frame, unclipped, with a 3.4s hold on them — the previous run's defect is fixed. It holds at 3 on a vocabulary collision and a dominant-read problem. The tile reads '4 Distributions not covered', but the calendar's own COVER column calls exactly ONE row 'uncovered' (Biu, Aug 1); the 4 is 1 uncovered + 3 at risk. A supply lead who counts what the table calls uncovered gets 1 and concludes the headline is wrong. Separately, eight of the ten fully-visible calendar rows are green 'covered', so the frame's dominant message is 'this network is fine' — the opposite of the scene's argument.
fix_recommendation: Rename the tile to match the table's own vocabulary — 'Distributions at risk or uncovered' — or make the calendar default to sorting the four exception rows to the top so the tile and the table agree at a glance.

scene: scene 1 — The organisation that feeds the children sees the least
detail: The model is legible end to end and genuinely closes a loop — a thin site offers 'Raise a shortfall', the raised state persists in place ('Raised Jul 24, 2026') and reappears as a record with a status. It stays at 3 because the exception statuses are inert: no filter, no drill, no definition affordance, so the screen surfaces an exception it gives the user no way to operate on from the place it is surfaced. The at-risk / uncovered threshold rule has no legend, tooltip or info bubble anywhere.
fix_recommendation: Make the status pills filter toggles that collapse the grid to the exception set, each with an 'i' affordance stating the rule verbatim ('uncovered = arrived stock below cartons required; at risk = covered only by consignments not yet received').

scene: scene 1 — The organisation that feeds the children sees the least
detail: Clean numerals, consistent card shells, tight column alignment and a clear H1/label/body distinction; host chrome intact and grounding. Three product-side notes keep it at 3: the KPI row has three different card anatomies (card 1 has no sub-caption and a dead band at its base; card 3 wraps to two lines, card 4 to one), so the row's baselines do not align; the panel description runs ~140 characters per line in low-contrast grey; and two adjacent columns carry byte-identical values in every row.
fix_recommendation: Give all four KPI cards the same anatomy with a reserved sub-caption line so baselines align, constrain the panel description to a ~75ch measure and raise it one contrast step.

scene: scene 1 — The organisation that feeds the children sees the least
detail: The declared narrated subject — the .keyfigures row — is fully in frame, unclipped, painted and settled, and the trace confirms the scene waited on that exact selector and held 3.4s. This is the previous run's biggest framing defect, now fixed. It stays at 3 because the frame is not composed around its subject: the four cards occupy the top ~18% while ~60% of the pixels go to a distribution calendar this scene's narration never mentions, and the Aug 4 Gwoza row is bisected at the viewport edge with a half-drawn pill as the frame's closing visual. A stray mouse cursor is baked over the nav pill.
fix_recommendation: After wait_for(.keyfigures), scroll_to the key-figures row and hold so it sits in the upper-middle third with only the calendar heading trailing beneath, and park the pointer off-canvas before the capture.

scene: scene 1 — The organisation that feeds the children sees the least
detail: The load-bearing figures land cleanly — 'eleven feeding sites' maps to the '11 Feeding sites' card and 'they know their caseload to the child' maps to CHILDREN EXPECTED per dated distribution — and the underlying data is unusually well reconciled (11 KPI = 11 rows in the cover table; thinnest cover 0 wk = Biu; 1 shortfall = the one Askira row; the stock chain carries correctly across dates, e.g. Monguno 840 − 532 = 308 → at risk on Aug 9). The residual is tense: 'they report a shortfall by telephone' and 'the one with no instrument to do it' are spoken in the present tense over a screen with a 'Raise a shortfall' control and a dated, status-tracked shortfall record. As an overview scene the pre-product framing is legitimate, but the grammar makes the frame contradict the words.
fix_recommendation: Tense-mark the pre-product clauses: 'They USED TO learn a consignment was late when a truck did not arrive... UNTIL NOW they have had no instrument to do it — this is that instrument.' One sentence, no new footage, and it converts the contradiction into the reveal it was designed to be.

scene: scene 3 — Weeks of cover, and the date it runs dry
detail: The strongest data card in the run — the derivation is stated on screen, all eleven weeks-of-cover values reconcile exactly to it on independent recomputation, and the ranking is worst-first and monotonic. Two caps hold it at 3. (1) The colour bands (red under 2, amber 2-4, green 4+) do not encode the only thresholds the card states ('at four weeks you plan; at one you triage') — red-to-amber switches at 2.0, not 1.0 — and there is no legend or info bubble, so colour asserts a band the reader cannot verify. (2) Mixed precision in the single load-bearing column: '2', '3', '4' render bare while 0.6 / 1.6 / 2.5 / 3.5 / 4.5 / 5.5 carry one decimal. Also: ten identical dark-green 'Raise a shortfall' primary buttons give Dikwa (5.5 weeks, 38 days out) exactly the same call-to-action weight as Biu (0 cartons), inverting the urgency the pills encode.
fix_recommendation: State the band definitions where the colour is used (a small legend or per-pill tooltip: 'under 1 wk triage / 1-4 wk plan / 4+ wk covered') and make the pill boundaries match the thresholds the subtitle already states; format the weeks column to a fixed one decimal and decimal-align it; demote 'Raise a shortfall' to a secondary control that escalates to primary only below the stated triage threshold.

scene: scene 3 — Weeks of cover, and the date it runs dry
detail: Nothing is incoherent — each row's urgency has a matching action, the already-raised row correctly swaps its button for 'Raised Jul 24, 2026', and that shortfall reappears below with matching site and date. Held at 3 by two affordance gaps: ten identical primary CTAs give no weight hierarchy, and the action column is unlabelled. Substantively, the card excludes inbound consignments the app already knows about ('+94 later' for Askira, '+141 later' for Biu) and discloses that exclusion only on the OTHER card, so a reader of this card alone sees 'Biu 0, awaiting first consignment' with no hint that stock is already booked. There is also no lead-time or next-receipt column, so '11 days' is not actionable without knowing whether resupply takes 5 days or 20.
fix_recommendation: Add the exclusion to this card's own footnote ('excludes consignments not yet received; see the distribution calendar for scheduled arrivals') and extend the row with an inbound column ('+94 due Aug 3') plus resupply lead time, so 'runs dry in 11 days' resolves to act-or-don't without leaving the table.

scene: scene 6 — From a batch to the child who recovered
detail: The idea lands in about three seconds without narration — the WHO bands behind each series plus the labelled '125 mm · recovered' line make 'food reached this child and their arm measurement climbed out of the red' self-evident, and this is the run's most compelling frame. It holds at 3 on a site-attribution mismatch: the trace clicks the Monguno Nutrition Centre row, and every visible child in the resulting panel is DIK-* (Dikwa), with all eight Monguno children below the fold. There is no site column, no grouping header, no filter, and nothing states that the ID prefix encodes the site — the only tie back to Monguno is a clause buried mid-sentence in the header prose. A viewer takes the fourteen visible Dikwa children to be Monguno's.
fix_recommendation: Add a site column (or a site group header) to the outcome list and order it by the site that was clicked, so the row a user acted on is the content they land on.

scene: scene 6 — From a batch to the child who recovered
detail: The core interaction is coherent and the trace confirms it fired: click a distribution row, get the batch that supplied it with its children, and the arithmetic ties out at every level (280 + 231 = 511 fed; 14 + 8 = 22 sampled; counting the status pills gives exactly the stated 18 recovered). Two things keep it at 3: the click-to-result mapping is off (Monguno row, Dikwa content, no site column or sort on a 22-row list), and the panel is a one-hop dead end — the spec's show block promises 'the consignment it arrived on, the distribution it fed, and the children admitted on it', but SHP-2026-0201 and both distributions are inert prose, so a chain the concept sells as walkable is walkable exactly once, in one direction.
fix_recommendation: Make SHP-2026-0201 and each named distribution clickable from the modal header so the chain resolves in both directions, and add site/outcome filter chips above the 22-row list.

scene: scene 6 — From a batch to the child who recovered
detail: The band-behind-sparkline device is a genuinely good idea, the row grid aligns cleanly, values are right-aligned and whitespace breathes — and the statistical caveat is restraint, not editorialising, so no editorialising cap fires. Held at 3 on density and colour: 21 of 22 sparklines carry no axis reference (only the focused row shows the 115/125 mm lines), so the layout invites a cross-row comparison the encoding cannot support; the focused chart is ~90px tall against ~55px for the rest and the flat 102→102 'Non Response' line does not sit where an absolute 98-134 mm domain would put it, suggesting per-row y-scaling; the fifth row — the first non-recovered case — is bisected mid-chart at the scroll boundary; and the loudest element on an evidence screen is a heavy primary-green button whose only job is to dismiss it.
fix_recommendation: Pin one shared y-axis with the 115/125 mm threshold rules spanning the whole column so all 22 series sit on one comparable scale, keep the focused row's height equal to the rest, and demote Close to a tertiary control.
